risks: We face competition and could lose market share to competitors due to rapid technological changes.
Spire's single UK manufacturing facility could cause production interruptions due to damage or failure.
Compliance with laws and regulations imposes added costs and may prevent future operations.
Spire received a notice from NYSE for not timely filing a Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q.
Spire may need to expand facilities as it grows and expects additional expenses.

growth_drivers: Spire Global signed MoUs with Schaeffler AG and Diehl Defence to build and advance space capabilities.
Spire successfully received data from its Hyperspectral Sounder demonstrator satellite.
Spire launched its seventh Optical Inter-Satellite Link satellite.
risks: Spire incurred significant restructuring and legal fees, impacting its financial results.

growth_drivers: Spire collects and transmits data from its LEMUR satellites.
Spire Global announced the launch of AI weather models built on NVIDIA Omniverse Blueprint for Earth-2.
Spire plans to invest in satellite design and manufacturing to improve satellite life and reduce latency.
risks: Delays in U.S. federal government orders due to macroeconomic conditions may impact revenue recognition.

growth_drivers: Spire secured a $5 million contract and an 8-figure opportunity from NOAA.
Spire secured RFGL awards from 4 new international customers in the second quarter.
Spire's partnerships with Schaeffler and Diehl Defence reflect growing interest in commercial space capabilities.
Spire is tracking over $100 million in U.S. federal pipeline opportunities.
Spire's core revenue expanded both year-over-year and sequentially, marking the strongest core revenue quarter since the divestiture.
Spire expects an 8-figure contract to be awarded in the next month.
Spire has signed new international customers and re-signed existing ones, contributing to growth.
Spire expects awards that will positively impact 2026 revenue.
Most of the capacity increase is from new satellites being launched.
